ut_goatland_wall.blurb: Goatland Wall is a limestone sport wall in the East Hellgate section of the Hellgate Cliffs, up Little Cottonwood Canyon. All 14 routes are bolted: one sits at 5.9, ten are 5.10, and three reach 5.11. The climbing leans on pockets and edges. You get there by hiking uphill from the canyon road and traversing past a couple of neighbouring walls, so expect a steep walk in before any climbing. It suits climbers who are comfortable leading around the 5.10 mark.

ut_portwoods_wall.blurb: Portwoods Wall is a limestone sport crag in Ophir Canyon, on the west flank of the Oquirrh Mountains, roughly a mile below the old mining town of Ophir with the cliff close beside the road. Its 14 bolted routes span 5.8 to 5.12, and 5.10 is the most common grade. The stone is fractured, with fewer pockets than American Fork, so a helmet is sensible, especially on routes that see little traffic. Despite the roadside position the place feels quiet and secluded.

ut_recess_the.blurb: The Recess is a trad-only crag in the Uinta Mountains of northeast Utah. Its 14 routes are protected entirely by removable gear, since no bolts have been placed, not even at the tops, so you need to be comfortable building your own anchors. Grades run from easy fifth class up to 5.11, with a cluster around 5.7 and a smaller group of 5.10s and 5.11s. Most of the climbing sits in the shade. Bring a standard rack plus extra webbing or a cordelette.

ut_tatooine.blurb: Tatooine is a limestone sport wall in the Galaxy Area of Rock Canyon, in the southern Wasatch. It holds 14 bolted routes from about 5.7 to 5.11, with the heaviest concentration between 5.9 and 5.11. To find it, continue along the main canyon trail past the Endor Wall and look for the big orange arch; the wall lies up from the Bug Barn wall, right of the Waterfall Wall. A couple of lines here are multi-pitch.

ut_temple_the.blurb: The Temple is a sport crag in American Fork Canyon in the southern Wasatch, with 14 bolted routes from 5.8 to 5.12 and a strong showing of hard 5.12s alongside several 5.10s. It differs from the canyon's usual steep, pocketed walls: the angle runs from just short of vertical to slightly overhanging, with delicate face climbing on small edges plus some arete and dihedral moves. The crag faces north and gets little direct sun, which makes it a summer option. There is no real trail, only a faint path up a loose gully, and rocks can come down it.

ut_goldenfingers_wall.blurb: Goldenfingers Wall is a small crag in Ferguson Canyon with 14 routes, most of them trad, plus a couple of bolted lines and two top ropes. Grades start at fourth class and reach 5.12, with 5.10 the most common. The canyon is a popular summer spot, since the small crags face north and are shaded by big trees, which keeps the climbing cool. Expect short canyon-style routes in a shaded setting rather than a big-wall day out.
